run_summary: Editorial review kept the Miyazaki Typhoon No. 24 update as a publish candidate after tightening its wording. The routine conditional Suwanosejima ash forecast was moved to WATCH because it does not describe a newly confirmed eruption or traveler-operational change.

candidates.title: Typhoon No. 24: JMA Urges Strict Vigilance for Landslides in Miyazaki
candidates.formal_status_basis: The cited item is JMA weather information. The headline describes the agency's call for vigilance without upgrading the bulletin itself to a formal English warning or alert label.
candidates.what_changed: The Japan Meteorological Agency's Miyazaki Local Meteorological Office issued weather information urging strict vigilance for landslides as Typhoon No. 24 and a front affect the region.
candidates.why_it_matters: Travelers in or heading to Miyazaki should use current JMA, local-authority and transport-operator information because conditions may change quickly.
candidates.traveler_action: Check JMA and local guidance before setting out, and verify current airline, rail and bus status directly with each operator.

candidates.title: Suwanosejima Volcanic Ash Forecast for September 5, 2026
candidates.formal_status_basis: The source is a scheduled volcanic ash forecast describing conditional dispersal if an eruption occurs.
candidates.what_changed: JMA published a scheduled volcanic ash forecast describing possible ash and small volcanic-rock dispersal if an eruption occurs.
candidates.why_it_matters: The information may matter to people already near Suwanosejima, but the cited forecast does not itself establish a newly confirmed eruption, a new access change or a new transport impact.
candidates.traveler_action: Monitor the latest JMA volcanic information and local guidance if traveling near Suwanosejima.
